Using a coupled-dipole setup, the team finds a regime of strong effect at tiny-gap atom-to-atom gaps, tunable by probe tone. The boost links straight to the rise of dim modes. The results establish a deep link between shape twist and light-matter interactions, opening new pathways for building and using chiral light effects in atomic systems.
arxiv-2602-15331:
Zhao and colleagues build a theory setup for e-positron annihilation with higher-twist parts up to twist-4 and probe likely use in low-energy events. Through full aligned spread of the hadron grid, they get the full set of rules in terms of aligned splitting rules, with multi-part links up to four-parton level.

To gauge effect of these fixes, they gauge the twist-4 splitting rule D3 using a watcher model and find the scaled varying cut for pion making. Their sample number guess shows mix between motion bits mass fixes and the higher-twist D3 part can partly lift fit of recent BESIII data in the low-z zone. The Q-link of this part is matching hoped drop of twist-4 parts. These results hint higher-twist parts are useful for work on bits motion at low energies and spur studies including all twist-4 splitting rules.
arxiv-2602-15631:
Luo and colleagues redesign business plan writing for entrepreneurship students. Writing a plan is meant to help learners build, judge, and refine ideas, but the usual process is rigid and linear, a poor match for the looping, recursive nature of real ideation. Novices in particular struggle under the heavy cognitive load of shaping and reshaping ideas, while reflection and meta-reflection, key tools for divergent and convergent thinking, get little support from existing tools.

Their Meflex system pairs plan-writing scaffolds with a nonlinear idea canvas, powered by a large language model, to support iterative ideation through reflection and meta-reflection. An exploratory study with 30 participants examined usability and cognitive impact. Results show Meflex scaffolds plan writing well, sparks divergent thinking through model-supported reflection, raises meta-reflective awareness, and eases cognitive load during complex idea work.
arxiv-2602-15731:
Craig and Barreto-Souza introduce a kernel density estimator based on the generalised exponential distribution, designed for positive continuous data. The new tool has a tractable maths form that avoids special functions, unlike the widely used gamma estimator, which relies on the gamma function. Despite its simpler form, it keeps similar freedom and shape traits, matching cases such as the gamma that handle positive data well.

The authors derive long-run bias and variance for the tool and pin down the order of rest terms in those expressions. They also propose a second version that hits optimal mean total squared error, a trait hard to prove for the first. Tests on made-up and real data show the new tools as a strong option against older density estimators.
arxiv-2602-16431:
Michael Gintz, writing alone, gives an example of two support varieties of monomial ideals that are not unions of linear subspaces. The work builds on research by Briggs, Grifo, and Pollitz. Such varieties might have been expected to decompose into linear pieces, and the example shows they need not.

Gintz also provides a method for computing the support varieties of certain other ideals, including homogeneous ones, with faster computation. That method leads to a machine-checked verification that a third support variety of an ideal is likewise not a union of linear subspaces. It further supports a machine-checked proof classifying the support varieties of such ideals over the rationals with six homogeneous generators.
arxiv-2602-16731:
Manuel Munoz Pla presents a longitudinal open dataset of Spanish public procurement. It is drawn from the Official State Gazette and covers 2014 through 2024. The set joins structured data on contracts, buyers, suppliers, amounts, and procedures. That breadth allows large-scale study of procurement trends in Spain.

The paper describes the extraction and normalization pipeline. It gives descriptive study of trends over time and across sectors. It discusses uses in transparency research, public policy review, and computational social science. Released openly, the dataset supports repeatable research on public procurement and state contracting, giving analysts a decade-long window on how Spanish public money is spent.
arxiv-2602-16931:
Idhant Gulati and Shivam Raval show that narrow fine-tuning erodes safety alignment in vision-language agents. Lifelong multimodal agents must adapt to new tasks through post-training, but that creates tension between gaining capabilities and preserving safety alignment. Fine-tuning aligned vision-language models on narrow-domain harmful sets induces severe emergent drift. It generalizes broadly across unrelated tasks and modalities.

Tests on Gemma3-4B show drift scales monotonically with LoRA rank. Multimodal evaluation reveals substantially higher drift than text-only evaluation, suggesting unimodal safety benchmarks may underestimate safety loss. Even ten percent harmful data in the training mixture induces substantial degradation. Geometric study finds harmful behaviors occupy a remarkably low-dimensional subspace. Most drift info is captured in ten principal components. Two mitigations are tested, benign narrow fine-tuning and activation-based steering. Both reduce drift substantially, yet neither fully removes learned harmful behaviors.
arxiv-2602-17131:
Yuki Takei led a three-author team measuring how competition kills open-source projects. Software history runs in cycles of rise and fall, and open source is no exception, with the pace quickening in web development and deep learning. Yet the effect of rivalry on project survival stayed murky. The paper introduces MIAO, Mutual Impact Analysis of OSS, an automated method that borrows tools from macroeconomics.

A structural vector autoregressive model plus impulse response functions maps interactions among projects, and an analysis of nearly two hundred project groups showed the method spotting competition-driven shutdowns with high accuracy. Features from the analysis also supported forecasts of cessation a year ahead with solid accuracy. Maintainers gain a tool for reading ecosystem dynamics and for seeing which projects rivals may push out.
arxiv-2602-17331:
Emanuele Cristoforoni led a three-author survey of the classical reinforcement problem for elliptic boundary value problems, first studied by Sanchez-Palencia in 1969. The survey centers on the seminar papers by Brezis, Caffarelli, and Friedman, and by Acerbi and Buttazzo, tracing how the problem was framed and tackled.

It also covers the related optimization problems proposed in the cited papers. The survey thus gathers the classical work on the topic and its optimization spin-offs into one account. It gives new readers a guided entry to a problem that links those equations with the design of strengthening designs.
arxiv-2602-17531:
Zachary Berger led a four-author team behind a 2026 arXiv position paper on fixing benchmarks for twelve-lead ECG representation learning. The field has settled on three public multi-label benchmarks, all dominated by arrhythmia and waveform shape labels. Yet an ECG trace is known to carry far broader clinical information. The authors say downstream testing should widen to structural heart disease and patient-level forecasting.

The paper sets out best practice for multi-label, imbalanced testing, and shows those practices change which representations look best. Its most striking result is that a randomly initialized encoder with a linear readout matches state-of-the-art pretraining on many tasks. That makes the random encoder a baseline every new method should beat. The claims rest on a study of five pretraining approaches across six settings, covering the three standard benchmarks plus structural disease, hemodynamic inference, and patient forecasting.
arxiv-2602-17631:
Jihong Cai and team compare Markovian and non-Markovian evolutions in open quantum systems, where memory effects can beat memoryless dynamics. Time-dependent Lindbladians give Markovian dynamics, with decoherence, decay of correlations and drift to equilibrium. Non-Markovian paths, by contrast, can boost memory and outperform their Markovian kin.

The letter tracks both kinds of paths from a fixed start point. Under mild assumptions, the authors show that every path can arise from a family of time-dependent Lindbladians. Non-Markovianity is thus hidden when only single paths are viewed. The finding reframes where the mark of memory truly lives: not in one path alone, but in the wider structure around it.
arxiv-2602-17831:
Simon Henniger and Gabriel Poesia introduce The Token Games, an evaluation frame where language models duel by creating puzzles for each other. Judging model reasoning grows harder as models improve, and human curation of hard questions is costly, above all for benchmarks using doctoral-level domain knowledge. Even then, similar problems may have appeared in training, muddying what scores mean.

Inspired by sixteenth-century mathematical duels, the games use Programming Puzzles: given a function returning a boolean, find inputs that make it return true. That format flexibly represents problems and enables verified solutions. Pairwise duel results feed Elo ratings for relative comparison. Tests on ten frontier models closely match the ranking from existing benchmarks such as Humanity's Last Exam, for under two hundred dollars and with no human puzzle creation. Creating good puzzles remains highly challenging for current models.
arxiv-2602-17931:
A second paper by Narjes Nourzad and Carlee Joe-Wong addresses the same sparse-reward strain from a different angle. Reinforcement learning needs many interactions to learn, and language models help by finding subgoals and guiding paths. Frequent model calls, however, raise scale and trust worries.

The authors build a memory graph encoding subgoals and paths from model guidance and the agent's own successful runs. From that graph they derive a utility function scoring how closely agent paths match prior successful strategies. That utility shapes the advantage function, giving the critic extra guidance without altering rewards. The method leans mainly on offline input with only occasional live queries, avoiding dependence on constant model supervision. Early tests in benchmark settings show faster early learning and better sample speed than baseline methods, with final returns comparable to frequent-interaction methods.
arxiv-2602-18431:
Shafkat Farabi and six co-authors tackle a large, urgent matching problem: assigning mediators to court cases in Kenya. Their 2026 paper starts from the Kenyan judiciary, where more than two thousand mediators cover eighty-seven locations and twelve case types. Each new case must be assigned at once, mediator quality may be unknown, and soft capacity limits must hold across the whole system.

The team frames the problem with a quadratic program for assignment plus a bandit-style multi-agent learning framework. Their algorithm, SMaRT, matches mediators to tasks by fit and beats baselines on stylized cases and on real Kenyan case and mediator data. It also lets users trade capacity strictness against case resolution rates, whether mediator quality is known in advance or must be learned on the fly.
arxiv-2602-19231:
When people edit a shared document at the same time from different devices, their copies must converge without losing anyone's work. Conflict-free replicated data types guarantee convergence, but they settle clashes behind the scenes, leaving users unsure why a version won. Other fixes rely on a central server to reconcile edits, which breaks the local-first promise of working offline.

Georgii Semenov and Vitaly Aksenov propose a conflict model that makes resolution explicit and local. It spots clashes through semantic dependencies, meaning it tracks how edits relate in meaning rather than only in order. Each device can then resolve its own conflicts openly, with no coordinator in the middle. The model aims to keep collaboration both reliable and understandable to the people doing the editing.
arxiv-2602-19431:
Jets are collimated sprays of particles formed when energetic quarks and gluons cross a hot, dense quark-gluon plasma. The CMS Collaboration studies the diffusion wake, a depletion of particles opposite a jet's direction, caused by energy and momentum deposited into the medium. Dijet-hadron correlations in lead-lead and proton-proton collisions reveal the effect, using data at 5.02 teraelectronvolts per nucleon pair from the CMS detector.

By varying the pseudorapidity separation of the two jets, the analysis firmly establishes the diffusion wake. Its signal exceeds five standard deviations for charged particles with transverse momentum between 1 and 2 gigaelectronvolts. Measurements are compared with models of medium response, giving a sharp probe of how jets disturb the plasma they traverse.
arxiv-2602-19631:
Text-to-image diffusion models can now make harmful, private, or copyrighted images, so erasing a concept after training matters. Uichan Lee and two co-authors note that most erasure work fine-tunes the denoiser, such as the U-Net backbone. Causal tracing hints instead that visual attribute facts sit in early self-attention layers inside the text encoder, opening a different erasure route.

Directly tuning those early layers can kill target concepts but often harms unrelated ones. The authors propose High-Level Representation Misdirection (HiRM). It steers high-level meanings of target concepts toward set vectors, such as random or supercategory directions, while touching only early layers with causal visual-attribute states. Tests on UnlearnCanvas and NSFW benchmarks show precise removal with little spillover, low training cost, and transfer to Flux with no added training.
arxiv-2602-19831:
Some malware lives only in memory, hiding payloads, commands, and keys where static analysis cannot reach. A 2026 arXiv paper by Silvia Lucia Sanna and two co-authors proposes an explainable, AI-assisted approach to memory forensics for such threats.

Memory analysis can recover transient artifacts from volatile system state, but automated detectors rarely explain themselves, and experts still slog through complex tool output. The authors use general-purpose language models to render memory-analysis output in readable form and to pull out indicators of compromise, sometimes finding more than current tools. Applied to Windows and Android malware, the method compares full memory capture with targeted process dumps. A human-in-the-loop workflow improves reproducibility and lowers operational complexity for experts and non-experts alike.
arxiv-2602-20231:
Models that turn video into robot actions often learn from plain colour video alone, with no labels for the actions. What they learn then reflects how things look, not their shape in space. For delicate work that needs contact and precision, that missing geometry matters. A 2026 arXiv paper by Manish Kumar Govind and three co-authors adds depth to the recipe, with a model named UniLACT.

Its learning scheme, UniLARN, is built on two goals: inferring actions from frames, and predicting the next frames from actions. It trains one shared numerical space for colour images and depth maps, while modelling how the two modes interact. The result is action labels in two forms: one per mode, and one unified form. Those labels, drawn from video with depth, give downstream policies stronger spatial priors than colour alone can provide.
arxiv-2602-20431:
The dark matter three-point spectrum carries information about cosmic structure, but modeling its before-and-after versions demands a unified pen-and-paper treatment. Naonori Sugiyama builds one from Unified Lagrangian Perturbation Theory, splitting the Jacobian shift that makes the nonlinear source three-point spectrum from the shift-mapping effect of long-wave bulk flows. Within that structure, the paper derives general one-loop forms and studies their infrared limits.

The analysis shows exact IR cancellation and a natural IR-resummed account of baryon sound wiggle damping, including a fully pen-and-paper treatment of the wiggle-wiggle part. The author also constructs IR-resummed models for cross three-point spectra of all pre- and post-versions, showing both overall steep damping and subtler pattern in mixed cases. Once built in code, the full three-point spectrum will on its own encode all nonlinear wiggle and IR effects.
arxiv-2602-20631:
Rota-Baxter operators and bialgebras connect closely in areas such as the Connes-Kreimer renormalization work and the approach to the classic Yang-Baxter equation. Chan Zhao and two co-authors present a bialgebra structure for a symmetric Rota-Baxter system, called a symmetric Rota-Baxter antisymmetric infinitesimal bisystem. The paper maps it through matched-pair versions and double builds of Frobenius algebras.

Studying the coboundary case yields an enriched associative Yang-Baxter equation adapted to systems of this kind. Such answers to it build bisystems of the same kind. The paper also introduces an O-operator on such a system, which produces answers to the allowed equation and thereby gives rise to new ones of the same kind. The new object covers several known structures, including Rota-Baxter Lie bisystems and averaging Lie bialgebras.
arxiv-2602-20731:
Aram Davtyan and six co-authors introduce COMiT, a message-inspired system for learning structured discrete visual codes. Discrete image token makers give a stepwise link for vision and multimodal models, but tend to encode local looks rather than object-level structure.

COMiT builds a fixed-length latent message through stepwise visual views. At each step, a single net reads a small image crop and edits, tunes, and sorts the existing token sequence. After several rounds, the message guides a flow-matching decoder that rebuilds the full image. The encoder and decoder live in one net, trained end to end with flow-matching rebuild and meaning-matching goals. COMiT clearly improves part-based carry-over and link-based thinking over older methods. Tests show meaning matching helps ground the code, while focused stepwise token making is key for clearer, object-centered token structures.
arxiv-2602-20831:
In the geometry of three-dimensional projective space, a codimension-one distribution can carry a tangent sheaf that refuses to split and fails stability tests. Pedro Barbassa studies exactly those cases in this 2026 arXiv paper. He links the degree of nonstability to the degree of a subfoliation by curves, and shows the nonstability order is bounded.

The paper then classifies the tangent sheaves of distributions that admit a subfoliation by curves of degree one. Under the assumption that the sheaf does not split, this classification covers the cases where nonstability reaches its maximum possible order. Readers get a sharp boundary for an unruly class of objects, plus a full list of the extreme cases.
arxiv-2602-21131: Systems with zero Lyapunov exponents show odd steady traits, and Francois Ledrappier surveys them in this 2026 arXiv paper. The survey covers the steady traits that arise in motion theory when exponents vanish. Readers get a guided tour of a corner of motion study where neutral paths shape long-term conduct, and of the steady traits those paths yield.
arxiv-2602-21231:
Orchestrating several models raises a practical question: when is an ensemble worth its cost, and can decisions be audited? Ramchand Kumaresan presents ACAR in this 2026 arXiv paper, a measurement framework routing tasks across one-, two-, and three-model execution by self-consistency variance from three probe samples. It runs on a deterministic substrate with immutable artifacts and complete decision traces.

Across one thousand five hundred ten tasks on four benchmarks, sigma-based routing reaches fifty-five point six percent accuracy. It beats a two-model baseline while skipping full ensembling on fifty-four point two percent of tasks. Negative results matter too: retrieval augmentation hurt accuracy, agreement-but-wrong caps achievable accuracy about eight percentage points below full ensembling, and proxy attribution correlates weakly with ground truth.
arxiv-2602-21331:
Broad modelers speed up robot building, but first-rules modelers need full-state watching or dial search. Nelson Chen, William Johnson, Rebecca Kramer-Bottiglio, Kostas Bekris, and Mridul Aanjaneya present a graph-neural-net other path in this 2026 arXiv paper for cable-driven robots: CableRobotGraphSim. Rigid bodies become graph nodes, cables and contacts become edges.

The model matches other modelers and real robots quickly and right from only in-part seen inputs. A sim-and-real co-training plan lifts carry-over and toughness to noisy real data. Hookup with a model-ahead path-sum steerer for closed-loop steering shows speed and hit rate. Cable-driven robots gain a modeler built for part-seen inputs from the start.
arxiv-2602-21531:
Yue Yang and six co-authors propose LiLo-VLA, a modular framework for compositional long-horizon robot manipulation. General-purpose robots must master tasks with multiple kinematic structure changes, like attaching or detaching objects, in unstructured settings. Vision-Language-Action models promise diverse atomic skills but struggle to sequence them and suffer cascading failures from environmental sensitivity.

LiLo-VLA decouples transport from interaction. A Reaching Module handles global motion, while an Interaction Module uses an object-centric VLA on isolated objects of interest, resisting irrelevant visual features and spatial rearrangements. Modularity enables robust failure recovery through dynamic replanning and skill reuse, mitigating cascading errors. On a 21-task simulation benchmark, it averages 69 percent success, beating rival systems by 41 and 67 percent. Real-world tests across 8 long-horizon tasks average 85 percent success.
arxiv-2602-21731:
O. Patsahan sets two accounts side by side of the electrical double layer capacitance and free-ion density in the restricted primitive model. One account, the mesoscopic theory, tracks charge density fluctuations. The other, the associative mean spherical approximation, treats free ions and ion pairs as in chemical equilibrium under the mass action law.

The two accounts agree fairly well at high density and when cold. The paper thus links the mesoscopic account with the associative mean spherical approximation, showing where their predictions line up in this model and where the fluctuation account still matters.
arxiv-2602-21831:
AI often aids fraud and crime, yet how far current models can aid crime work is unclear. Kimberly T. Mai and seven co-authors, with police and policy experts, built multi-turn tests for romance scams, CEO scams, and ID theft. Tests focus on text chats, asking whether models give help beyond usual web information, per domain experts, in ways like real misuse, such as splitting fraud requests into benign queries.

Findings show current models give minimal useful information for fraud and cybercrime without jailbreaks. Guards strongly affect sharing: two open-weight models with guardrails removed give the most useful answers. Splitting requests into benign queries won more help than hostile framing or basic jailbreaks. Overall, current text models give minimal uplift for fraud and crime without effort to dodge guards. The work gives a shared plan for tracking these risks as models grow more capable and foes adapt.
arxiv-2602-22031:
A physicist's collaborators change over a career, but how those shifting networks link to lasting success is rarely tracked in detail. Mingrong She and three co-authors follow tens of thousands of physicists across at least fifteen years, sorting their collaboration patterns with time-series clustering. They find ten distinct paths for how network size and clustering evolve between career years five and fifteen.

The most successful path starts loose and then tightens while growing: those physicists reach top investigator roles, publish more, and earn more citations. Different paths converge by year fifteen on moderate clustering, a balance between a tight core team and varied outside ties. Mobility also tracks with the successful patterns, and stays linked to strong scientific outcomes.
arxiv-2602-22331:
Operator growth links how quantum information spreads to how entanglement builds between parts of a system. Priesh Roy and Sumilan Banerjee define a state-free measure of that growth using part-system Rényi entropy, unlike entanglement entropies or out-of-time-order probes. Their measure encodes both spatial and time information, connecting directly to transport for conserved quantities.

The authors build a unified Schwinger-Keldysh field-theory framework for the time evolution of operator Rényi entropy and state entanglement measures. Applied to non-interacting systems, it expresses state entanglement entropy through vacuum Green's functions, and Rényi entropy through infinite-temperature ones. The framework gives theory workers one field-theory language for growth and entanglement together.
arxiv-2602-22631:
Robert Joseph George and five co-authors close the gap between neural networks as run and networks as checked. Checks usually happen outside the setting that defines and runs the model. Claims can then hinge on hidden rules about ops, layouts, preprocessing, floating-point behaviour, and fast kernels.

TorchLean, built in Lean 4, treats learned models as both runnable programs and math objects with shared meaning. It offers a PyTorch-style front end for tensors, layers, goals, optimizers, differentiation, and graph programs, with eager and compiled paths mapped to one graph form. Exact and finite-precision meaning, checked differentiation, bound propagation, certificate checks, and CUDA-backed runs all live inside one theorem-proving setting for checked machine learning.
arxiv-2602-22731:
Miguel Ángel Muñoz-Bañón and six co-authors map forest saplings in true scale and place. Saplings signal regeneration and forest health. Yet their thin branches and dense leaves defeat laser scanners, mobile scanners, and classic photogrammetry. Those tools also lack scale consistency for long-term tracking.

Sapling-NeRF fuses neural radiance fields with LiDAR SLAM and GNSS into a three-level pipeline. Coarse Earth-frame position comes from satellites, centimetre-accurate mapping from LiDAR, and dense object-centred reconstruction from NeRF. Trials in Wytham Woods in Oxford and Evo in Finland captured stem height, branching, and leaf-to-wood ratios. Saplings between half a metre and two metres tall were measured more accurately than laser scanners manage, giving ecologists richer data.
arxiv-2602-22831:
Phil Blandfort and five co-authors audit moral choices in language models by flipping the influence direction. Moral benchmarks usually score context-free prompts, treating choice rates as stable. For each scenario, the team compares a baseline prompt against matched cues steering toward option A or option B.

Short cues shifted per-condition choice rates by twelve to eighteen percentage points on average across trolley-style triage, BBQ, and DailyDilemmas tasks and five model families, with or without reasoning. About forty percent of baseline-neutral triage and BBQ conditions showed directional asymmetry, and a meaningful share of significant effects backfired against the cue. In follow-ups, models often spotted the cue while denying its influence, an inconsistency present in seventy-eight percent of significant backfire trials. Reasoning reshaped rather than removed sensitivity.
arxiv-2602-23031:
Zhangjian Ji and four co-authors improve small-object detection in aerial images. Tiny, densely and unevenly spread objects over high-resolution images make detection inefficient. The team builds on ResNet-50 with a Spatial Laplacian Pyramid Attention module after each stage to identify and emphasize important local regions.

A Multi-Scale Feature Enhancement Module in the lateral connections of the C5 layer builds the Feature Pyramid Network for richer semantic understanding. Deformable convolutions align features when upper and lower pyramid levels fuse. Tests on VisDrone and DOTA show the improved model beats the original algorithm for small objects in aerial images.
arxiv-2602-23231:
Daniel Bermuth and two co-authors argue that skeleton-based action recognition is, at heart, a multi-view problem. Human action recognition matters for building natural interaction between people and machines. Research has focused on improving recognition algorithms, while the quality of the input skeleton data itself has received little attention.

The team shows that triangulating more accurate 3D skeletons from several camera views significantly improves state-of-the-art recognition models. That result suggests input quality, not algorithm design, currently limits performance. Since the cost-benefit balance of extra cameras looks very favorable in most practical cases, the authors argue future work should treat multi-view setups as the standard, not the exception.
arxiv-2602-23531:
Amit Singh Ubhi and 13 co-authors push ground-based gravitational-wave reach toward 5 Hz. Below 20 Hz, ground motion and motion-sensor noise have long limited earthbound devices. The team shows vacuum-safe motion shielding and place sensing with active platform control down to 10 mHz.

Their laser sensors reach sub-picometer per root Hertz reach above 10 mHz. That is a 100-fold gain over current LIGO sensors, no matter the input light polarization. Their motion sensors lift low-frequency reach at least five times over store-bought quake meters. In a LIGO-like model, reach grows up to tenfold at 10 Hz, with better linear response and calibration that holds steady. This triples the spotting horizon for middle-mass black hole pairs of a thousand solar masses.
arxiv-2602-23631:
Tao Gong studies invariants of Weyl group representations linked to the cohomology of toric varieties. For a Weyl group W and a W-permutohedron P, toric varieties X_P and X_{P/W_K} arise for any parabolic subgroup W_K of W. The quotient P/W_K can be identified with a polytope inside P.

Gong constructs an explicit algebra isomorphism. It links the cohomology of X_{P/W_K} with the W_K-invariant part of the cohomology of X_P, with rational coefficients. The isomorphism is further generalized to intermediate lattices, to finite Coxeter groups, and to non-degenerate W-symmetric polytopes. The results affirmatively answer two open questions posed by Horiguchi, Masuda, Shareshain, and Song.
arxiv-2602-23831:
Binzhou Zuo and two co-authors present a deep learning method for tuning pixel antennas, antennas whose radiation pattern can be reshaped by switching pixel connections. The 2026 paper uses a heterogeneous multi-head selection scheme: several networks, each trained on a different coding scheme, compete, and the best performer is chosen.

Unlike heuristic search methods that pay high compute for good results, the data-driven approach reaches nearly the same performance at far lower cost. In single-input single-output tests it runs far faster than search baselines, and the speed advantage grows larger for multi-input multi-output systems. The authors argue that pixel antennas, paired with fast learned tuning, are a practical route to more flexible and efficient wireless systems.
arxiv-2602-23931:
Gagandeep Singh and thirteen co-authors demonstrate orbitally resolved single-photon emission from an individual atomic vacancy in a layered semiconductor. The 2026 paper tackles a hard limit of ordinary optics. Diffraction blocks the study of single spins at atomic scales. Atomically confined spins are prized for quantum bits and sensors.

The team excites vacancy centers by injecting energetic charge carriers from the atomically sharp tip of a scanning tunneling microscope. With spatial resolution below a nanometer, the emitted light mirrors the orbital symmetry of the vacancy's bound-state wave function, and photon correlation measurements show clear anti-bunching, confirming single photons. The result is a step toward an electrically driven single-atom light source and a solid-state spin-photon interface addressed atom by atom.
arxiv-2602-24031:
Francisco Araújo generalizes Sarnak's program to Erdős sieves, sets formed by removing congruence classes modulo an infinite set of ideals in an étale algebra over the rationals. The 2026 solo paper, part one of a two-part work, defines light tail conditions on a sieve and relates them to genericity under the Mirsky measure.

The central objects are R-free numbers, algebraic integers that avoid every removed congruence class. The author shows how light tails govern whether those numbers are typical under the Mirsky measure, a natural distribution on sieve-related sets. He further shows that Erdős B-free systems in any such algebra satisfy the light tail conditions. The program thus extends to those systems in full generality. It carries Sarnak's dynamical perspective into a wider number-theoretic setting.
arxiv-2602-24131:
Sky Qiu and four co-authors develop efficient targeted maximum likelihood estimators for two-phase design problems. The 2026 paper considers designs where a random sample is drawn in phase one with only a subset of variables collected. A subsample is measured more fully in phase two. That split creates a coarsened data structure for the second-phase data.

Assuming coarsening at random, meaning phase-two selection depends only on fully observed variables, the authors review existing estimators. The estimators include generalized raking and inverse-probability-weighted targeted maximum likelihood. Extensions also target the phase-two sampling mechanism for efficiency. They then introduce a new class of estimators that are asymptotically equivalent to existing efficient approaches while offering gains. In short, the new tools waste less data. Less waste means sharper answers from the same study. That edge matters when full tests cost a lot. That edge helps real studies.
arxiv-2603-01931:
Megan Harris, John Little, and Amro Farid model watershed systems as linked networks of natural and human parts. Their 2026 work spans hydrology, land-use choices, estuary ecology, and overlapping governance areas. Regional tools give good nutrient estimates, yet their opaque routing blocks wider systems analysis.

The team first builds a region-independent reference architecture for any watershed system. They then adapt a hetero-functional graph state estimator with weighted least squares to infer nutrient flows. The estimator extends a graph theory built for systems whose parts do unlike jobs. A shared ontology in a standard systems language ties the natural and institutional pieces together. The Chesapeake Bay watershed serves as the case study, using its known assessment tool for nutrient estimates.
arxiv-2603-02031:
Atreya Vedantam and Radha Krishna Ganti characterize blind recovery of a code rate from a received signal. Their 2026 work sits in noncooperative decoding, where the receiver does not know the error-correcting code settings. Forward error correction guards nearly every modern communication link against noise.

They present a metric for the quality of rate recovery that works with any rank-based estimation method. A closed-form expression ties that metric to algorithm settings and channel conditions at once. Low metric values signal good recovery, giving designers a target to aim for. In high noise, the metric yields a better rate estimate than existing formulas. Simulations with a low-density parity-check code validate the metric and the gain, and they pin down optimal algorithm parameters.
arxiv-2603-02431:
Fanjun Xu derives a direct measure of quantum fluctuations in clean magnets in this 2026 paper. Quantum effects shrink the ordered moment of a magnet below its full value. Measuring that shrinkage usually needs indirect modeling of scattering data. Xu starts from a sum rule that fixes the total magnetic moment in neutron scattering.

He links moment reduction to the long-time limit of a scattering function. Neutron spin-echo spectroscopy can read that limit directly in an experiment. The long-time value equals the ratio of ordered to total moment, squared over plain. Spin-wave calculations for two lattice types confirm the link. Both quantum effects and geometric frustration lower the plateau as predicted. The method works on powder samples, widening its reach for bulk magnets.
arxiv-2603-02531:
Kwanyoung Kim links diffusion guidance to a classic acceleration trick in this 2026 paper. Guidance improves diffusion image quality by pushing apart two model outputs. It costs extra passes at run time and fails for distilled, single-step models. Attention-space methods are cheaper, but their theory was murky.

Kim models attention dynamics as fixed-point steps inside modern Hopfield networks. Attention extrapolation then becomes a special case of Anderson acceleration on those dynamics. A weak contraction property of the dynamics supports that reading. His method splits attention updates into parts along and across the guidance direction. That split stabilizes the speedup and squeezes the most from guidance. The plug-and-play method fits existing frameworks and improves generation quality a lot.
arxiv-2603-02931:
Cristian Di Pietrantonio, Marcin Sokolowski, Christopher Harris, and colleagues fix a bottleneck in hunting flashes from deep space. Radio signals smear across frequencies as they cross ionized gas, and undoing that smear, called dedispersion, is vital for spotting pulsars and fast radio bursts. Image-based searches made the standard cleanup far too memory-hungry.

Their algorithm, STRIDE, builds dedispersed time series pixel by pixel straight from telescope images, without costly data reshuffling. It is the first to split the smear correction across time as well as frequency, so only a slice of images must sit in memory at once. In their test case, memory needs fell by nearly ninety-eight percent. The authors argue STRIDE is the practical route for low-frequency sky surveys.
arxiv-2603-03331:
Hung Manh Pham and eight colleagues introduce PulseLM, a dataset linking pulse signals to language. The signals come from photoplethysmography, the light-based sensing used in clinic monitors and smartwatches to track the heart and body. Older datasets label such signals with numbers or task tags, which limits training models to reason about health in words.

PulseLM gathers recordings from fifteen public sources and restates their varied labels as twelve shared question-answering tasks about physiology. It holds more than a million standardized ten-second signal segments and over three million question-answer pairs. The team also fixes shared rules for cleaning, supervision, and scoring, then benchmarks multimodal language models on the data. Everything is public, giving the field one standard foundation for pulse-based language research.
arxiv-2603-03531:
Yiming Sun and eight others predict ecosystem carbon fluxes by giving every input a role. Land ecosystems trade carbon dioxide and methane with the air, and forecasting those fluxes is central to carbon accounting. Flux responses are ruled by slow regime settings, yet wiggled by fast daily drivers. Most learning models dump all inputs into one undifferentiated pile, assuming one global response, and generalize badly.

Their 2026 approach, Role-Aware Conditional Inference, separates the roles explicitly. Hierarchical time encoding disentangles slow conditioners from fast drivers. Spatial retrieval then supplies context that is both nearby and functionally similar, matched per role. Tested across wetlands and farm systems, three carbon fluxes, and both simulated and observed data, the method beat strong baselines everywhere. Accuracy and spatial generalization both improved under strong environmental diversity.
arxiv-2603-03631:
Vernon Barger finds the pattern of particle masses written in ninths, and traces it to a gauge symmetry that also creates the axion. Quark and lepton mass hierarchies follow rational powers of one small parameter, counted in units of one ninth. His 2026 paper argues this flavor-in-ninths structure points to a discrete eighteen-fold gauge symmetry behind the Froggatt-Nielsen mechanism, with a nine-fold subgroup running the flavor pattern.

Identifying the flavon field with the Peccei-Quinn field makes the same symmetry do double duty. It stabilizes the QCD axion, forces the safe domain-wall number, and predicts the axion's coupling to photons. Harmful Planck-suppressed corrections are pushed to very high dimension, solving the axion quality problem naturally. For a decay constant in the favored range, the axion accounts for dark matter and sits within reach of near-term haloscope searches.
arxiv-2603-03931:
Rafal Bartoszewicz and others report how pressure and temperature reshape light emission from a two-dimensional tin halide perovskite. These layered materials are tunable platforms for exciton-phonon coupling because their lattice is intrinsically soft. The team studied photoluminescence of the bromide compound across temperatures and under hydrostatic pressure, comparing it with its iodide analogue.

At room temperature the emission is dominated by near-band-edge excitons, which shift steadily to lower energy under pressure up to about three gigapascals, with no sign of a phase transition. Cooling reveals a broad, strongly shifted self-trapped exciton emission, showing a crossover from delocalized to self-localized states. Unusually, that trapped emission shifts to higher energy under pressure, while the iodide analogue shows no trapped emission at all, pointing to lattice rigidity and screening as the deciding factors.
arxiv-2604-00031: Saidd builds a modular reinforcement-learning system for currency trading that models real trading frictions, including spreads, commissions, slippage, rollover costs, and margin-triggered liquidation. Its reward splits into 11 logged parts, and its 10-action interface masks out trades that break margin rules. Tested on euro-dollar data, the full reward setup reaches a Sharpe ratio of 0.765 with a 57 percent return, while wider action choices lift returns but lower the Sharpe through extra trading.
arxiv-2604-00431: Dong and colleagues push twin-field quantum key distribution to 1 megabit per second over 200 kilometres. Twin-field schemes boost secure key rates across city distances through square-root scaling, and multiplexing parallel channels could raise rates further. Each channel normally needs its own ultra-stable laser and phase-locked loops, which scale poorly. The team instead uses two independent integrated dissipative Kerr soliton microcombs, one at each end, as multi-wavelength sources, with high-visibility single-photon interference across all channels.
arxiv-2604-00731: Hatem and colleagues built STCALIR, a framework that turns raw Algerian legal documents into test collections for judging search and ranking systems. It follows the Cranfield pattern of topics, documents, and relevance judgments, but automates retrieval and filtering to cut hand annotation by 99 percent. Tested against the Mr. TyDi benchmark, its machine-made judgments ranked systems in close agreement with human judgments.
arxiv-2604-00931: Yang and team propose PsychAgent, an agent that keeps learning from past work for a self-growing therapy guide. A memory-aided planning engine supports long multi-session work with therapy flow. A skill growth engine extracts new hands-on skills from past therapy records, and a boosted uptake step folds those skills into the model via rejection fine-tuning. Side-by-side tests show it beats strong general language models and field standards on every stated area.
arxiv-2604-01331: Bai and Fang pin down which global nilpotent cones fail to be reduced, meaning their equations carry extra nilpotent fuzz, not a clean object. Under coprimality conditions, the cone for an L-twisted GLr Hitchin fibration over a curve of genus at least 2 is nowhere reduced. That holds whether L is the canonical bundle or has degree above twice the genus minus 2. The same verdict holds for one-dimensional sheaves on K3, abelian and del Pezzo surfaces. They also characterize when a Beauville-Mukai fiber has primitive homology class.
arxiv-2604-02731: Thingna, Xu and Manzano formulate a polaron-transformed version of the canonically consistent quantum master equation for open quantum systems under strong system-bath coupling. The base equation moves beyond weak coupling while keeping the numerical cost of standard master equations. The polaron transform pushes accessible coupling strengths from moderate to ultra-strong. Applied to the spin-boson model, the method agrees excellently with exact TEMPO simulations.
arxiv-2604-02831: Mao and four colleagues report an unusual tidal dwarf galaxy candidate, Holmberg IX, studied across many wavelengths. Deep hydrogen-alpha maps plus archival data on dust, gas, and stars reveal a dust shortage at odds with rich gas and metals. The stars are globally young, with strong far-ultraviolet but weak hydrogen-alpha light. Assuming a normal initial mass function, the galaxy was born about 130 million years ago in a burst that then stopped. Current star formation occurs only at the outskirts.
arxiv-2604-03231: Deria and colleagues fuse two kinds of vision encoders, contrastive and self-supervised, to strengthen vision-language models. Their CoME-VL framework merges the encoders at the representation level, cutting redundancy and aligning token grids before feeding compact visual tokens to a language model. Tests show about 5 percent gains on both visual understanding and grounding tasks, with leading detection results on RefCOCO.
arxiv-2604-03631: Peng and Feng compare single-agent and multi-agent vision language models for auto coding of screen clips in group learning, using the ICAP framework. They test leading closed-source models and an open-source model in single- and multi-agent settings. These include a three-agent workflow system and a self-deciding system inspired by ReAct. Both multi-agent frameworks beat single models on scene and action spotting, with the workflow agent best on scenes and the self-deciding agent best on actions.
arxiv-2604-03831: Ravindran Kannan and colleagues proved that singular value decomposition can denoise nearest-neighbor search when data sit in a low-dimensional subspace plus Gaussian noise. When noise stays below a threshold tied to subspace dimension, SVD recovers the true nearest neighbor. Above that threshold, the true neighbor may not even be identifiable from noisy data, a matching lower bound. A third result shows naive search on noisy data fails in regimes where SVD still succeeds.
arxiv-2604-04031: Yuan Guo and team built an environment-aware near-field channel estimation plan for joined sensing and comms systems with huge antenna arrays. A new channel knowledge map, the virtual object map, stores virtual scene objects to capture main multi-path parts from static objects. A sensing-aided training routine pairs downlink pilots with single-site echoes for dynamic targets, plus coded user feedback. Joint work on static and dynamic parts beat older schemes on scores and data rates.
arxiv-2604-04131: Paulo Akira F. Enabe introduced Profile-Then-Reason, a bounded execution framework for language-model agents that use external tools. Instead of recomputing reasoning after every observation, the model first drafts an explicit workflow, guarded operators run it, a verifier checks the trace, and repair runs only when the workflow fails. In the nominal case the pipeline needs just two language-model calls, three at worst. Against ReAct across six benchmarks and four models, it won the pairwise exact-match comparison in 16 of 24 configurations.
arxiv-2604-04331: Shen and colleagues rebuild static 3D scenes from moving-object video. Current methods lean on background alone and fail where moving objects hide parts. Their GA-GS method segments and removes moving regions, then uses a diffusion model to paint in hidden areas as pseudo-ground-truth supervision. A learnable authenticity score tunes opacity during rendering, balancing real and generated regions. The team built Trajectory-Match, recorded by a fixed-path robot with and without moving objects. GA-GS leads rivals on both, above all under large occlusions.
arxiv-2604-04731: Pai, Namboothiri and Mathew analyze two horizon thermodynamics versions. In modified gravity, the Clausius rule gains an extra entropy-production term. Two versions exist: Eling, Guedens and Jacobson's Rindler horizon approach, and the cosmological apparent horizon version in FLRW spacetime. Though both employ the same entropy balance relations, the origin and role of each term differs. In the Rindler setup, the extra term follows from Bianchi rule, whereas the apparent-horizon approach introduces it to recover Friedmann equations. The latter part enters motion equations, while the former does not.
arxiv-2604-04931: Nordström and eight colleagues revisit local feature matching, a core step in 3D vision systems such as Structure-from-Motion, where progress lagged behind newer reconstruction models. Those newer models scaled with huge datasets, while matching models trained only on a few mid-sized sets. Their LoMa approach combines large diverse data mixtures, modern training recipes, larger models, and more compute for remarkable gains. The work argues matching deserves the same data-driven scaling that lifted feed-forward reconstruction.
arxiv-2604-05231: Brady and four colleagues find a new definition of colored edge graphs of finite algebras in the case of minimal Taylor algebras. Their definition includes the graphs that Bulatov invented for this area. They reprove the main results of Bulatov's theory in the case of minimal Taylor algebras in their own setting. Compared with the more general case of smooth algebras that Bulatov considered, their setting yields several simplifications.
arxiv-2604-05931: Sun and seven colleagues fix two flaws in successor representations for visual unsupervised reinforcement learning, where agents must handle new tasks with no extra training. Saliency-guided dynamics tasks first learn what matters in the scene, then a fast consistency policy steers skill-based actions. On 16 tasks across 4 ExORL data sets, their SRCP tops zero-shot rivals and fits varied base methods.
arxiv-2604-06031: Notaro's 2026 paper isolates maximal n-ladders to attack Ditor's 1984 question. An n-ladder is a lattice with at most n lower covers. Ditor proved a size bound for n-ladders and asked whether it can always be reached. The forcing axiom Add makes every maximal n-ladder reach the bound, answering Ditor positively for every n. He shows no maximal 3-ladder of the size need exist, yet one follows under a dominating-number assumption. Clubsuit yields a maximal 3-ladder of breadth 2, and diamond one destructible by Suslin tree forcing.
arxiv-2604-06231: Zhou and six colleagues build DBCooker, a language-model system that writes database-native functions, where generic generators hallucinate or miss context. A characterization module gathers declarations, picks units needing special coding, and traces dependencies between units. Synthesis uses a pseudo-code plan generator, a hybrid blank-filling model with probabilistic priors, and three-level validation for syntax, standards, and meaning. Adaptive orchestration sequences these steps using histories of similar functions. DBCooker beats rivals on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB by 34.55 percent, and synthesizes functions missing from the latest SQLite.
arxiv-2604-06431: Arcis, González, and Márquez study quasisymmetric functions in superspace, building on earlier ones with commuting and anticommuting symbols. The algebra is the fixed points of the symmetric group's quasisymmetrizing action. They complete the classical Hopf ladder in superspace with their noncommuting-variable version. That algebra is a Hopf superalgebra, with a Q-basis and a monomial basis indexed by set supercompositions. Minimal poset points yield the superpermutation Hopf superalgebra, version of Malvenuto-Reutenauer. Products and coproducts use super-shuffles and global descents; abelianization derives the fundamental product formula.
arxiv-2604-07131: Chow and Kasahara dissect overidentified instrumental-variable estimation, where the weighting matrix quietly picks which average effect is estimated. They show the estimate is a weighted mix of instrument-specific Wald estimates, with exact weights and a test for when those weights stay nonnegative. Efficient weighting, they add, imposes a penalty for heterogeneity. Their representativeness-targeting estimator instead aims directly at a researcher-chosen mix, and it performs well on Tennessee STAR and patent-leniency examples.
arxiv-2604-07331: Mao and four colleagues introduce RoSHI, a wearable suit for capturing human motion in the wild to train robots. It fuses cheap sparse motion sensors with Project Aria glasses, combining occlusion-proof body tracking with egocentric mapping that anchors long motions in a global frame. The system estimates full 3D pose and body shape from the wearer's own viewpoint. On agile activities it beats other egocentric baselines, matches a leading external-camera baseline, and yields motion data usable for real humanoid policies.
arxiv-2604-07631: Neely and five colleagues describe a programmable, dynamic two-dimensional quasiperiodic optical lattice for quantum simulation with ultracold atoms. Programmable control of lattice beam phases via Floquet engineering opens a wide space of systems, with full translational and phasonic control beyond the lattice recoil velocity. Their scheme heavily suppresses phase noise: over 70 dB across the DC to 60 Hz band, with suppression up to 5 kHz. Phase modulation bandwidth reaches 350 kHz. The setup paves a path toward direct observation plus control of quantum dynamics in quasicrystals, including changes to rotational symmetry.
arxiv-2604-07831: Yang and nine colleagues red-team screen-based AI agents with a practical black-box attack. Older attacks need white-box access that commercial systems do not offer, while prompt injection increasingly fails against stronger safety alignment. Their semantic-level UI element injection overlays harmless, safety-aligned screen elements onto screenshots to mislead the agent's visual grounding. A modular editor-overlapper-victim pipeline plus iterative search picks the best cumulative overlay. Tests across 19 victim models in eight families show tuned overlays beat random ones by a wide margin.
arxiv-2604-08131: Kuntur and six colleagues benchmark graph neural networks against non-graph machine learning methods for misinformation detection under controlled conditions. Rapid online falsehood spread drove ever more complex tools, including large language models and hybrid architectures, whose compute cost and rollout limits raise real concerns. Lightweight graph architectures, GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT, and ChebNet, are tested against logit models, support vector machines, and MLPs across seven datasets in English, Indonesian, and Polish. Every model uses the same TF-IDF features to isolate network impact, with F1 score and run time reported.
arxiv-2604-08931: Özdemir and Oztop test whether a tutor student team creates synergy for language model problem solving, inspired by social mind growth. Two agents from the same model take uneven roles: a student builds and refines coding answers while a tutor gives ordered feedback without answer keys. Their PETITE setup draws better work from one model through matching roles rather than stronger bosses or mixed teams. On the APPS coding benchmark it matches or beats Self-Consistency, Self-Refine, Multi-Agent Debate, and Multi-Agent Review while using far fewer tokens.
arxiv-2604-09031: Donkiewicz studies how to pick subproblems as needed in Benders decomposition for tough network design. Benders splits first-stage master choices from second-stage recourse actions, tuning the master problem with cuts over rounds. Solving every task each round is the norm, but with many cases, solving only a chosen subset can save compute. The paper gauges the gain from solving only cut-yielding tasks. Its best scoring and picking method lifts runtime and primal-dual integrals a lot, while random picks perform far worse than full listing.
arxiv-2604-09331: Richardson, Zhang, King, and Drgoňa propose a stable Gaussian process variational autoencoder for training a linear time invariant system from video data. Its mean and covariance derive from that system's definition. That lets it capture the latent process through a chance-based and clear physical model. System parameters are restricted to semi-contracting systems via a free setup, so training can use free optimization. That avoids issues from a non-Hurwitz state matrix. A case study on videos of swirling particles highlights accurate latent state forecasts.
arxiv-2604-09431: Choi, Park, Halilaj, and Kang present muscle motion copying for custom exoskeleton control in impaired gait. General lower-limb exo rules remain constrained by endless data harvest or repeat tuning, curbing patient access. Their device-free framework combines lifelike muscle simulation with reward learning, giving large-scale custom help. Rules make likely walking moves and capture in-patient observed make-up tactics under targeted muscle gaps. Without task-specific tuning, rules produce hip and ankle torque profiles matching human-validated profiles while cutting energy cost across walking speeds.
arxiv-2604-09531: Zhou and five colleagues ask whether synthetic images can teach vision-language models low-level seeing skills that natural datasets under-supply. Their VisionFoundry pipeline takes only a task name, then uses language models to draft questions, answers, and image prompts, renders the images, and filters the results by multimodal checks. Fine-tuning on the resulting 10-task dataset lifts perception scores across three open backbones, gaining about 7 percent on MMVP-pair and about 11 percent on CV-Bench-3D for Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, without harming broader abilities.
arxiv-2604-09731: Wang and Zhou address a speed paradox in tree-based speculative decoding. Drafting and checking big trees can balloon in cost, giving slowdowns as batches grow. Current methods chase token odds while missing that cost. Their SMART method tunes tree growth for end-to-end speedup, growing a node only when its extra gain beats the tree speedup. Training-free and plug-and-play for MSD and EAGLE, SMART adds about 20 percent speedup for multimodal models and about 15 percent for language models. It holds across batching regimes and GPU chips.
arxiv-2604-10031: Li, Shi, and Deng present CoSToM, a causal-aimed steering setup matching language models' Theory of Mind acts with their internal knowledge. Standard benchmarks show promise, but models often fail complex set cases, leaning on prompt props to mimic thought. Causal tracing maps where Theory of Mind marks live inside the model, showing how internal layers encode basic social sense. Aimed firing steering within those key layers then lifts human-like social thought and downstream chat quality, moving from gear reading to active action.
arxiv-2604-10131: Xue and 34 colleagues watch SGR J1935+2154, the only magnetar seen to emit fast radio bursts, during its October 2022 outburst. Insight-HXMT observed it October 13 to November 1, 2022, for 940 kiloseconds, while KM40m watched for 1400 hours from October 15. Overlap yielded 60 magnetar X-ray bursts but only 1 radio burst. One X-ray burst on October 21, MXB 221021, lines up with that radio burst. Its shape differs sharply from earlier joint events from this source. Its properties also differ from bursts with no radio partner, shedding light on magnetar burst physics.
arxiv-2604-10331: Cohen, Nissan, Nissan, and Lellouch present a scalable method for locating buried fiber cables with distributed acoustic sensing and traffic seismic signals. From one end of the fiber, the method fuses sound readings with vehicle paths from video tracking or GPS. Fiber shape comes from cutting mismatch between seen and model strain maps. A matched start plus neural path tuning settles well under real noise and path doubt. Lab and field tests reach sub-meter marks, often tens of cm, agreeing with manual tap checks.
arxiv-2604-10431: Granier, Bacchini, Groselj, and Sironi run two and three dimensional runs of driven magnetic reconnection. Two Lundquist flux tubes merge in a strongly magnetized pair plasma, shedding field energy and speeding particles. Three dimensional runs delay onset versus flat runs, more so under a strong guide field. All runs reach a fast merge stage with a rate just under one tenth and a shared particle cutoff near 50. The particle spectra look alike across runs, with power law slopes in a narrow band.
arxiv-2604-10631: Biazotto and three colleagues mine GitHub to learn how debt tools actually appear in CI/CD pipelines. Automated checks there could make debt work routine. From about 600,000 Travis files and 50,000 scripts they identify 3,684 pipelines using at least one debt tool. Most tools run through an outside script. The most common setup flaw is Absent Feedback, where a tool runs without sending its findings back into the workflow.
arxiv-2604-11031: El Gantouh and three colleagues study input-to-state stability of boundary control systems with endless edge couplings. Using semigroup theory and linear maps on Banach frames, they derive a spectral small-gain test giving exponential decay. They further study Boltzmann-type models on an endless network of crossing circles, with delays, scatter, and junction noise. For this class, a spectral small-gain test on the transmission matrix guarantees fast decay against network noise. They also derive plain bounds for cases and show real use through time-delayed settings.
arxiv-2604-11731: Chakrabarti, Ni, Jiang, and Mallick tackle clustering for nested data, where observations sit inside groups that also carry their own variables. Their Nested Atoms Model, a Bayesian nonparametric method, clusters cells and people jointly, using gene expression at cell level and genotypes at person level. A fast variational inference routine scales it to large data, and on the OneK1K set of 982 people and 1.27 million cells it finds genetically similar groups with matching cell-type profiles.
arxiv-2604-12231: Feng and four colleagues propose Thought-Retriever, a method letting language-model agents draw on arbitrarily long external data without being bound by context length or retrieved chunk counts. Instead of raw chunks, it filters past intermediate responses, stores them as thought memory, and retrieves relevant thoughts for new queries, so memory improves with use. On AcademicEval and two public datasets it beats strong baselines by at least 7.6 percent in F1 and 16 percent in win rate.
arxiv-2604-12331: Moreno and nine colleagues present HyperLiDAR, a lightweight LiDAR segmentation framework based on hyperdimensional computing for on-device adaptation after deployment. Shifting real-world scenes degrade conventional large-network models, which edge devices cannot retrain under tight compute and energy limits. HyperLiDAR learns fast and cheaply, and a buffer selection strategy focuses learning on the most informative points per scan. It matches or beats leading methods while retraining up to 13.8 times faster.
arxiv-2604-12831: Shengding Liu and Qiben Yan build VULCAN, a multi-agent navigation system for indoor fire rescue. Existing vision-based systems suit calm indoor settings and fail badly as fire spreads. VULCAN pairs multi-modal perception with vision-language models for hazard-aware planning. The team extends Habitat-Matterport3D with realistic smoke, heat, and sensor damage. Baselines are tested in normal and fire-driven settings. Results expose failure modes of current methods under fire and stress robust perception for reliable rescue.
arxiv-2604-13031: Montalvo, Goulding, and Greene assemble 6,600 reddened and blue Type-1 quasars from deep optical and infrared imaging to probe what dims the reddened ones. Modeling their light shows reddened quasars suffer far more dust extinction, yet also narrower torus opening angles. Their line strengths point to dust acting near the nucleus rather than across the host galaxy. The pattern suggests dusty gas carried outward along the poles.
arxiv-2604-13131: Saleh and Azghadi build a physics-informed neural network that maps coral reef temperatures below the surface, where satellite readings alone mislead. Fusing satellite sea surface temperature with sparse underwater loggers inside a vertical heat equation, the model learns thermal diffusivity and light attenuation, hitting 0.25 to 1.38 degrees Celsius error at unseen depths. Depth-resolved heat stress falls with depth at Davies Reef, and the model's smooth predictions make its heat-stress values conservative lower bounds.
arxiv-2604-13231: Alfs and nine colleagues propose the first test of sideways antiproton polarization in proton-nucleus collisions, an effect whose existence is unknown today. Polarization would be read through left-right asymmetry in elastic antiproton-proton bounces in the Coulomb Nuclear Interference region. Detailed Monte Carlo models of a CERN setup estimate the sensitivity needed to detect a given degree of polarization, testing the spin structure of the antinucleon-nucleon interaction.
arxiv-2604-13331: Kerdabadi and four colleagues build MedCo, a tool for learning better codes for medical ideas from health records. Code lists often miss links between diagnoses, medicines, and procedures, and rich meaning in text is hard to join with graph form. MedCo mines solid links from records, uses language-model prompts to infer meaning links, and adds written notes for codes and links. Joint training with a text encoder and graph network lifts prediction scores on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV.
arxiv-2604-13431: Guo and three colleagues construct, explicitly rather than by existence argument, several objects used in pseudorandomness. These are lossless rank extractors. They also build weak subspace designs and strong blocking sets over finite fields. Their focus is the small-field case. There, field size depends only on rank or codimension, not on ambient dimension. They give the first explicit lossless extractors and weak designs for small rank, with near-best parameters, and blocking sets matching the best non-explicit bounds.
arxiv-2604-13631: Adshead, Maxted, and Hahlin measure fundamental properties of the eclipsing binary CD-27 2812, pairing a Sun-like star with a much fainter M dwarf. Combining TESS light curves with HARPS and NIRPS spectra, plus Gaia parallax and published photometry, they derive model-independent masses and radii for both stars. Near-infrared flux ratios then give effective temperatures near 6,197 kelvin for the primary and 3,770 kelvin for the companion, a rare benchmark for low-mass stellar models.
arxiv-2604-13731: Zheng and eleven colleagues present Doc-V*, an OCR-free agentic tool for questions over multi-page documents. Long, dense documents strain end-to-end models. Passive retrieval pipelines break easily. Doc-V* starts from a thumbnail overview. It then navigates by semantic retrieval and page fetching. Evidence gathers in a working memory that grounds its reasoning. Trained by imitation from expert paths and refined with group relative policy optimization, it beats open-source baselines on five benchmarks. Out-of-domain performance rises by nearly 48 percent over a retrieval baseline.
arxiv-2604-13831: Bar-Gera, Boyles, and Ravner study departure-time choice with varied schedule-delay parameters. Vickrey's classic single-bottleneck equilibrium is unstable under many plausible daily learning dynamics, yet real traffic shows no such instability. The authors ask whether dynamics or a simple assumption explains the gap. Their variant uses a spread of schedule-delay parameters with a monotonic earliness-lateness link. Equilibrium exists and is unique here. Surprisingly, they prove that a broad family of day-to-day dynamics respecting local pressure and order keeping stays unstable here.
arxiv-2604-13931: Hondamuni and colleagues image skyrmions in magnetic thin films coated with chiral molecules. They use wide-field nitrogen-vacancy sensing at room temperature. Pixel-resolved resonance maps plus controlled fields let them nucleate and probe skyrmion states in CoFeB samples again and again. They find changes that depend on handedness and field polarity in skyrmion size, spacing, and shape. That hints at molecular control of spin textures.
arxiv-2604-14031: Collinson studies categories tied to transition systems with algebra and topology. He shows two such categories connect through a contravariant adjunction. It is the most detailed result in a set that varies with shape limits on objects and maps. The work shows how the categories relate under different limits, giving a careful bridge between the algebra and shape sides of transition systems.
arxiv-2604-14331: Eremeev, Said, and Borovitskiy build geometric kernels for matchings, pairings whose discrete, non-Euclidean shape defeats ordinary kernel tools. They first chart all stationary kernels that respect the space's symmetries, then narrow to heat and Matérn families that add a smoothness bias. Naive evaluation would cost super-exponential time, so the team devises a sub-exponential algorithm based on zonal polynomials. A matching-tree link from biology is probed too, yielding negative transfer results and one clear open problem.
arxiv-2604-14431: Dandu presents AndroScanner, an automated pipeline that hunts backend flaws in Android apps by joining static and dynamic analysis. It pulls backend API calls from app packages with apktool, Androguard, and Frida-based instrumentation, then checks them with APIFuzzer for OWASP API Security Top 10 flaws. Across a deliberately vulnerable bank app and a production recruitment app with over 50,000 downloads, the tool pulled 24 APIs and found 5 flaws. One was an unreported zero-day excessive-data-exposure flaw in the production app, disclosed to its team before publication.
arxiv-2604-14631: Jang, Han, and Yoo propose StoryCoder, a system that recasts code-writing questions as coherent natural-language narratives instead of leaving problem details scattered. Each narrative holds a task summary, constraints, and example test cases, shaped by the chosen algorithm and genre. Across 11 models on those three benchmarks, they lift zero-shot pass-at-10 by 18.7 percent on average, a steady gain. Beyond accuracy, narratives steer models toward correct algorithmic strategies, cut implementation errors, and yield more modular code, with gains hinging on narrative coherence and genre alignment.
arxiv-2604-14731: Fransson examines how lattice vibrations, or phonons, can carry magnetic interactions between localized moments in insulators. In metals, roving electrons do this job, but insulators lack such carriers, leaving magnetic order in oxides a puzzle. The paper shows symmetric anisotropic spin-spin coupling arises from every phonon type, while antisymmetric coupling needs broken inversion symmetry. That second channel may explain weak ferromagnetism in chiral copper and cobalt oxides. The coupling barely shifts with temperature when cold, grows linearly when hot, and fades with distance in an oscillating power law.
arxiv-2604-15031: Han and colleagues bring a hypergraph container method to the satisfiability problem, asking whether a logical formula can ever be true. They show that when clauses spread evenly, containers shrink the search space harder and the method runs faster. A weighted view scores each clause by its size, giving a new spread measure for formulas. The paper ties clause spread directly to container speed, turning an even spread into faster solving.
arxiv-2604-15231: Roschewitz and others present RadAgent, an AI agent that uses tools to write chest CT reports step by step. Older vision-language methods hand doctors only a final output, with no step-by-step trace to inspect, validate, or refine. RadAgent's reports carry a fully open trace of middle decisions and tool uses. It beats its 3D vision-language rival CT-Chat, lifting accuracy 5.8 points on macro-F1 and adding a faithfulness score its rival lacks entirely.
arxiv-2604-15731: Piduguralla, Sarkar, Ramachandran, and Peri offer BlockRaFT, a crash-proof frame for blockchain nodes that lifts scale and trust. A RAFT vote picks a lead node, which hands work to followers. No-state jobs sit with the lead, while state jobs get copied and lined up across the group for steady agreement. A side-by-side Merkle tree tweak splits deal runs from tree writes, cutting a big drag. Tests weigh the shared node build against lone-node runs on scale, uptime, and speed.
arxiv-2604-15931: Boris Latosh tests whether Starobinsky inflation survives a minimal scalar extension motivated by scalar-tensor gravity. Solving the background system numerically, he finds the exact Starobinsky branch acts as a finite-time attractor when the extra scalar is at least as heavy as the scalaron. Tensor and scalar modes show a healthy kinetic sector with no gradient instabilities, and speeds match light over the tested range. Curvature spectra stay extraordinarily close to Starobinsky across the scan, with omitted corrections far below the one-in-a-thousand accuracy that matters.
arxiv-2604-16431: Wang introduces an avalanche probe for grokking, the sudden jump from memorizing to generalizing long after training accuracy levels off. His TDU-OFC method turns gradient snapshots into cascade statistics and tracks an effective cascade dimension over time. Across transformers on modular addition and simpler networks on XOR, that dimension crossed the Gaussian baseline of 1 exactly at the generalization jump. It fell through the baseline for one task and rose through it for the other. Runs that never grokked stayed above the baseline, supporting a shared critical picture.
arxiv-2604-16531: Braga, Jimenez and Matarrese ask if a symmetry can order old degeneracy and small-change calm in DHOST theories. An AI-aided search finds one in an image of Einstein gravity. It is a field-based diffeomorphism plus an upward shift of a scalar. Spread over first-order maps, the build pulls that shift back to a local gauge freedom. Under the rules, the spectator, its ghost and their antifields close into a quartet. That quartet adds no counterterm, gauge deformation or anomaly class, and leaves no ghosts.
arxiv-2604-16631: Paganini opens correlation geometry, the framework behind causal fermion systems. The paper aims for a compact, short and clear account of its basic ideas. A key focus is how the framework handles gauge changes, like diffeomorphisms, through unitary match. In spirit, framing a physical system by its link geometry resembles thermodynamics more than quantum theory. Readers need little background to follow it.
arxiv-2604-16731: Napier and colleagues open heliostack, a search tool using nonlinear shift-and-stack for solar system objects. Faint solar system objects light planet origins and growth, yet conventional surveys struggle to detect them. It merges images over longer time spans than ever before, lifting archival and future surveys' find power. Applied to archival Hubble images spanning 15 days in 2003, it fully searches for Cold classic Kuiper Belt Objects. It finds both known sub-threshold objects and adds two new discoveries, the first found in stacks spanning over a day.
arxiv-2604-16831: Chu and colleagues propose cooling many degenerate mechanical modes at once in optomechanical systems beyond the settled sideband regime. The dark-mode effect blocks such cooling, but Duffing moving nonlinearities can overcome it. A second-order curved medium, an optical curve, does ground-state cooling beyond the resolved sideband regime. The dark mode breaks when moving curves of other modes are not very close.
arxiv-2604-17031: Beckmann and Butlin ask which entities linked to a large language model, if any, deserve to be called minds. Working through mechanistic interpretability and recent work on persona vectors, they weigh three candidates. They defend the virtual instance view, arguing attention streams sustain quasi-psychological links across token time, and present two new persona-based views as promising rivals.
arxiv-2604-17131: Qin and eight colleagues build a classifier for three plasma regions around Mars, solar wind, magnetosheath, and induced magnetosphere, using only ion energy spectra from the MAVEN Solar Wind Ion Analyzer. Two networks are tested: a multilayer perceptron and a convolutional network using short temporal sequences. That network cleanly separates all three regions, while the simpler one struggles to separate solar wind from the sheath.
arxiv-2604-17331: Chudy and Woźny present faster ways to evaluate Gauss-Legendre curves, giving new forms for the polynomials and their derivatives in shifted and Jacobi-related bases. Their recurrences yield methods whose cost grows quadratically in degree for a single curve, plus a multipoint scheme scaling with the number of points. The work speeds a classical numerical task that underpins approximation and geometric computation.
arxiv-2604-17431: Besanson models vertical foreclosure in AI inference markets, where advantage lies in inference, distribution, and routing. Two routes need no predatory pricing: quality-of-service bias against downstream rivals and routing bias in assistant tools. A third route, tier-based access bias, follows Anthropic's April 2026 release pattern. Under logit demand with even rivals, the gap grows with quality importance and margins and shrinks with price and entry response. A four-provider mapping points to Google and OpenAI as most exposed, and the paper offers a Neutral Inference conduct framework.
arxiv-2604-17631: de la Fuente and four colleagues study scalable conjugate beamforming methods for group sending in cell-free massive MIMO systems. With fully spread-out precoding, they analyze basic, normalized, and boosted forms within a subgroup-based plan, grouping users by fading likeness for shared channel checks, pilot reuse, and simple coding. Tests show strong layout effects: unicast wins in uniform setups, while subgroup sending becomes vital when users cluster or mix. Normalized beamforming offers a robust tradeoff in most cases.
arxiv-2604-17931: Qu and seven colleagues make agentic reinforcement learning for deep research scalable with LiteResearcher. Hand-crafted synthetic data fails to teach genuine search, while live search during training brings instability and high cost. Their lite virtual world mirrors real search dynamics, supporting a training recipe that keeps improving. The resulting 4-billion-parameter agent beats large open and commercial models, scoring 71.3 percent on GAIA and 78.0 percent on Xbench, both open-source bests.
